title: Meet the only known trebuchet casualty in history
gist: Paleopathologist Jo Buckberry identified 'Skeleton 150' beneath Stirling Castle as the only known trebuchet casualty in the archaeological record—a Scottish defender likely killed by a ~200-300 km/h projectile during Edward I's 1304 siege.

insights.claim: Researchers used forensics, X-rays, and micro-CT scans to conclude 'Skeleton 150'—whose skull broke in 61 places—died from a single crushing high-speed impact consistent with a trebuchet projectile, the only such case in the archaeological record.
insights.speaker: Kiona N. Smith
insights.quote: we believe this is the first evidence of trebuchet trauma in the archaeological record

insights.claim: The man was likely a Scottish defender killed during Edward I's 1304 siege of Stirling Castle, which used 13 siege engines bombarding around the clock for three months plus the massive 'War Wolf' trebuchet.
insights.speaker: Kiona N. Smith
insights.so_what: Medieval history color; no market relevance.
